key_insight: For pulmonary embolism risk stratification, medical records and cardiac biomarkers were more predictive than vascular information from CTPA, and graph neural networks on vascular trees did not outperform strong tabular models.
clinical_relevance: This suggests that in routine PE assessment, readily available clinical data may be more useful for risk stratification than adding complex vascular graph features from imaging alone.
method: Benchmarked tabular models using medical records plus cardiac biomarkers.
Added vascular biomarkers extracted from CTPA to test whether imaging-derived vascular features improved prediction.
Applied graph neural networks to the intrinsic vascular tree graph representation and compared them with strong baseline models.
evidence_signal: The study used a private cohort of 353 patients with complete data for PE risk stratification and found that vascular biomarkers and vascular-graph GNNs did not improve performance over tabular baselines.
watch_item: The dataset was small and private, so the negative finding may not generalize broadly without external validation.
paper_title: Pulmonary Embolism Risk Stratification from CTPA and Medical Records: Vascular Graphs Are Not All You Need
